activities.anchor: carries more diagnostic bits than any single test
activities.caption: call the history's share of the diagnosis
activities.name: dtHistoryEstimate

config.prompt: Classic clinical-teaching estimates put one stage alone at most of the diagnosis. Roughly what share belongs to the history?
config.why: About 80%, with examination and tests splitting most of the rest. Symptom timing is often the discriminator: thunderclap onset points to haemorrhage, hours of gradual build to inflammation, exertion-then-rest cycling to a flow problem.

config.root: Chest-pain triage: the differential ranks candidates by two criteria at once — likelihood and danger.

start.text: One candidate is reflux (very common). Another is aortic dissection — perhaps 1–2 presentations per thousand, lethal within hours, with a different emergency treatment. How do you rank dissection?

choices.label: Promote it up the ranking despite the rarity
choices.feedback: The profession's distinctive twist: danger ranks up rarity.

choices.label: Leave it low — far too rare to consider first
choices.feedback: Likelihood alone is only half the ranking rule.

promote.text: A "can't-miss" diagnosis is promoted deliberately: missing dissection costs hours, while the common candidate usually announces itself in the history. That is why the ranking is ordered by likelihood and danger together.

low.text: Ranked on likelihood alone, dissection hides — and the trade-off is written in hours. Can't-miss diagnoses rank up even when rare; that is what the second criterion is for.

fish.text: Testing follows the same discipline: each test is chosen because it can discriminate between the top candidates. A test that will not change management is not worth its own risks and costs — no scattershot panels.

config.why: Ranked by likelihood and danger; tested to discriminate, not to fish — that principle is what separates a targeted workup from a scattershot panel.

activities.caption: pair each exam pattern with its localisation
activities.name: dtLocaliseMatch

config.prompt: The neurological exam as localisation instrument — pair each pattern with its reading:

pairs.left: weakness with brisk reflexes and an upgoing plantar response (Babinski)
pairs.right: upper motor neuron lesion — brain or spinal cord, upstream of the anterior horn cell

pairs.left: weakness with wasting, flaccidity and lost reflexes
pairs.right: lower motor neuron lesion — anterior horn, root, plexus or peripheral nerve

pairs.left: right face and right arm weak together, right leg spared
pairs.right: left cerebral hemisphere's cortex — in the cord, leg and arm tracts run together

pairs.left: orthostatic blood-pressure drop; heart rate fails to rise on standing

config.why: Each pathway runs a known route, so a pattern of deficits localises the lesion before any scan — and re-examining an hour later shows whether a stroke is extending.

activities.anchor: three meanings, depending entirely on who is being tested
activities.caption: do the mammography arithmetic by hand
activities.name: dtBayesEstimate

config.prompt: Screen 10,000 women: prevalence 1%, sensitivity 85%, specificity 90% (so 990 false positives among the 9,900 disease-free). Of the ~1,075 positive results, roughly how many are true positives?
config.why: 85 of ~1,075 positives — a positive predictive value of about 8%. Nine of ten flagged women do not have cancer. Run the identical test where prevalence is 10% and the PPV lifts to about 43%: the test did not change, the population did.
config.context: Sensitivity and specificity belong to the test; predictive value belongs to the test plus the population.

activities.anchor: Formal versions of this reasoning use
activities.caption: file each rule under the right test property
activities.name: dtSnOutBuckets

config.prompt: Two working rules govern test direction — file each fact:

items.label: a highly sensitive test comes back negative — disease effectively excluded
D-dimer: extremely sensitive, poorly specific — the rule-out gate for clots
a negative D-dimer in a low-risk patient ends the workup
a highly specific test comes back positive — disease effectively confirmed

config.why: A positive D-dimer barely raises the odds and must be followed by specific imaging — likelihood ratios (LR+ = sensitivity / (1 − specificity)) shift the odds multiplicatively and let imperfect tests chain.

activities.caption: one line of the case reasoning reaches for the wrong rule
activities.name: dtOccamSpot

config.prompt: A case discussion — one line reaches for the wrong rule of thumb. Click it:
lines: Fast pattern recognition is legitimate expertise for routine presentations.
The referral note's phrase fixed attention, and later evidence was read through it — anchoring.
The process stopped at the first plausible diagnosis — the most common cognitive error in studies of diagnostic failure.
The patient is elderly and complex, so Occam's razor demands a single unifying diagnosis.
With an unstable patient, resuscitation precedes diagnosis — "sick or not sick" comes first.
config.correction: Hickam's dictum governs the elderly and the complex — patients can have as many diseases as they please. Occam's razor (seek one unifying diagnosis) is the counterweight for young patients with one coherent story.
config.why: The rules of thumb are scoped counterweights, each aimed at a known shortcut of the fast system.

activities.caption: true or false — the guardrails, audited
activities.name: dtGuardrailJudge

statements.s: Diagnostic error is a rare curiosity, confined to unusual diseases.
statements.why: A 2023 Johns Hopkins analysis estimated ~795,000 Americans die or suffer permanent disability from diagnostic error yearly; earlier outpatient work put it near one adult in twenty per year.

statements.s: Vascular events, infections and cancers account for about three-quarters of serious diagnostic harm.
statements.why: Stroke, sepsis, pneumonia, venous thromboembolism and lung cancer top the list.

statements.s: Checklists and structured templates work by making clinicians smarter.
statements.why: They make the fast system slow down at the known failure points — forcing the can't-miss items into view when the anchor says otherwise.

statements.s: Explicit pre-test probability scoring (Wells score, CHADS₂) makes the Bayesian step visible.
statements.why: Alongside decision-support systems that compute the likelihood ratios clinicians skip.

activities.caption: fill the expert layer's four refinements
activities.name: dtExpertCloze

config.text: Experts store diagnosis as organised %%0%% — classic presentation, risk factors, course, complications — so pattern recognition is fast script-matching. Chained tests are not %%1%%: proper analysis works in odds and %%2%% throughout. AI classifiers trained on enriched prevalence over-predict in the wild, so emerging best practice uses them as a %%3%% reader, not a first opinion.
config.hint: The first blank is what novices lack; the third is the multiplicative quantity; the last is a reading role.
